title: The distance unit is 'mileage' and the meter unit is 'hours', in full
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin, or a user with "Settings Service" enabled, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (it ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. A schedule open in the editor with the service form ready. Seed it:
  3. ↳ Settings > Maintenance > New schedule (or open an existing schedule and Edit).
  4. ↳ Click Add service to open the blank service form.
  5. On the service form, tick Distance and Engine hours so both units appear.
custom_steps:
1. Read how the distance unit is named wherever it appears.
  2. Read how the engine-hours unit is named wherever it appears.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The distance unit is the word "mileage", written in full wherever a unit is named; "mi" and "km" never appear.
  • Engine hours are written "hours" in full wherever the unit is named, never "hrs".

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10559 (S2, Add a routine service to a schedule); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S2; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R10: “There is one distance unit and its name is the word mileage, written in full wherever a unit is named. mi and km never appear: the single unit covers both, so an abbreviation would claim one of them”
  • S2-R15: “Engine hours are written hours in full wherever the unit is named, never hrs, on the same rule as mileage in S2-R10”

AUTOMATION: HOLD - not yet build-verified on a Maintenance Reminders QA build (feature ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag)
